newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 16.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* CBS Entertainment president Leslie Moonves assured the Hollywood creative community Tuesday that the new TV content code adopted by broadcasters last week "will not influence our programming one iota." CBS is a unit of Westinghouse Electric.
* Time Warner's Warner Bros said Tuesday the studio and Arnon Milchan's New Regency Prods have been unable to come to terms on a new production agreement.
* With a two-week gross of close to $140 million, Sony's "Men in Black" has been heralded as a box office savior, one of the few bright spots in a troubled summer.
* Fox's highly promoted firstrun summer series "Roar" got off to a noisy start Monday, winning its hour in homes, adults 18-49 and 25-54, and all key adult male demos.

* Actor Alec Baldwin's production company El Dorado Pictures has signed a two-year overall deal with Sony-owned Columbia TriStar TV and a second-look feature deal with Columbia Pictures, Columbia confirmed Tuesday.

* Gianni Versace -- arguably youngish Hollywood's favorite couture designer and a designing staple of premieres and Oscar parties for years -- was shot to death just steps from the front door of his South Miami Beach home Tuesday morning. He was 50.
